conviction_note: abs_move 22 (implied 18.1, own median 26.4, 6 of 8 prints beat the implied) at p_up 52. Two things roughly cancel. For an up move: the company has beaten the top of its revenue guide two quarters running, and the stock has fallen 22% in 5 days on a sector selloff, which lowers the bar. Against it: the last two beat-and-raise prints were sold (-38%, -13%), one customer is now 11% of revenue, and RPO fell in Q2. The findings sum to +0.6, close to the scaled +0.88; both say this is a lean, not a call.
bar: Q3 revenue $188.3m (Zacks consensus, https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:2a43909f5094b:0-fastly-set-to-report-q3-earnings-what-s-in-the-cards-for-the-stock/), with MarketBeat at $187.82m (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-11-4-fastly-inc-stock/). Two sources agree within $0.5m, inside the company guide of $184-190m. Non-GAAP EPS $0.12 against a guide of $0.11-0.13, non-GAAP operating income guide $20-24m, FY26 revenue guide $732-746m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001517413/000151741326000212/ex991-fslypressrelease63026.htm). The bar is sourced, so sizes are not capped.
positioning_check: Short interest 20.58M shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, about 3.7 days to cover, on 159.3M shares outstanding, so roughly 13% (massive.com snapshot of 2026-11-04 https://massive.com/quote/fsly). The 2026-09-30 figure was 21.19M, so shorts were flat to slightly lower. Trefis showed about 14% on 2026-10-09. That is elevated but below the 18-23% that squeezed on earlier days. The 25-delta skew is +4.54 vol points (puts bid, mild), put/call OI 0.76 and ATM IV 267%, and the baseline lean is 'downside paid'. The tape is -22.2% over 5 days and -16.8% over 20 days, 37% below the 52-week high, yet still up about 107-113% YTD.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue likely lands above the $188.3m consensus, near or above the $190m top of the guide. Q2 printed $183.3m against a guide of $170-176m ($7.3m, 4.1%, over the top), Q1 printed $173.0m against a guide that implied a flat quarter, and the Q3 guide midpoint of $187m asks for only +2% sequential growth after +6% in Q2. A repeat of the pattern puts Q3 near $192-195m, about 2-3.5% over the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats have been sold. Q1 2026 (2026-05-06) was a beat and raise and the stock moved -38.2% (baseline); Q2 2026 (2026-08-05) beat the guide top by $7.3m, raised FY and moved -12.9% (baseline). Earlier beats were bought: +72% (Feb 2026), +36% (Nov 2025).
findings.why_not_priced: The beat pattern itself is widely known (Zacks counts 4 of 4 EPS beats), so consensus sits at $188.3m, above the $187m guide midpoint and under the $190m top. If a beat to about $194m were priced, consensus would sit above the guide top and the stock would not have fallen 22% into the print.
findings.independence: Q1 revenue against its guide comes from the Q1 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001517413/000151741326000129/ex991-fslypressrelease33126.htm). The same company documents underlie the guidance finding below.

findings.finding: The FY26 revenue guide of $732-746m, with H1 at $356.3m and Q3 guided at $184-190m, implies Q4 of $191.7-199.7m. A Q3 near $193m would force a FY raise toward roughly $745-755m unless Q4 is guided flat. The Investor Day of 2026-09-22 set 2029 targets of $1.1-1.3bn revenue (14-21% CAGR), a 20-22% operating margin and a 12-15% FCF margin, which gives a framework for raising.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY guidance was raised in both May and August 2026 and the stock fell both times (-38%, -13%), reportedly on core network services deceleration in May. The Investor Day itself was sold, with the stock about -8% on the day (https://www.tikr.com/blog/fastly-fell-8-today-heres-where-the-stock-could-go-in-2026).
findings.why_not_priced: The Q4 that the guide implies is arithmetic anyone can do, so a modest raise is expected. What is not priced after a 22% fall is a raise in line with the run-rate. If it were priced, the stock would sit near the ~$28 of late September rather than $21.
findings.independence: Investor Day targets: https://quartr.com/events/fastly-inc-fsly-investor-day-2026_3gNKajyE. This shares the supplement with the reported-quarter finding; it is a different line (guide versus quarter).

findings.finding: Concentration and backlog are deteriorating under the growth. One customer was 11% of Q2 revenue (10% for H1), the top-10 share rose to 37% from 31% a year earlier, total RPO fell to $340.9m in Q2 from $368.7m in Q1, and the count of large customers fell to 624 from 634. Revenue is usage-based, and the 10-Q says changes in usage by the largest customers 'can create volatility in our revenue'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The May 2026 -38% came on a core network services slowdown despite a beat. Network services (73% of revenue) grew only 11% in Q1 2026 and 17% in Q2, while security grew 43-47%. A top-customer usage swing was historically the cause of large Fastly drawdowns.
findings.why_not_priced: The 11% single-customer figure sits in a 10-Q note, not in the press release, and the RPO decline was masked by a 38% year-on-year headline. If the market had priced it, the guide would carry a wider range or previews would mention it; the previews found mention neither. Net of the rest: security is growing 43% and is 23% of revenue, so a single-customer wobble would need to exceed roughly $5m a quarter to break the guide.
findings.independence: Large-customer count and RPO series come from the investor supplement (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001517413/000151741326000212/ex992-investorsupplement63.htm), the same company's documents, so this is not independent.

findings.finding: Capex has surged and cash conversion is thin against a maintained FY FCF guide of $40-50m. Capex was $24.8m in Q1 and $35.8m in Q2 (H1 P&E purchases $52.6m against $12.5m a year earlier), Q2 FCF was $3.6m and H1 FCF was about $7.6m, so H2 must deliver about $32-42m. The 10-Q flags component shortages and price increases. The $60m-to-$100m revolver upsizing of 2026-08-17 funds that network build, which NRR of 117% and RPO up 38% year on year corroborate, so the financing itself is signed neutral and the risk is to the FCF guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior on the FCF line for this name. The Zacks preview names memory shortages and higher opex as headwinds, and the Q3 non-GAAP operating income guide of $20-24m is below Q2's $27m.
findings.why_not_priced: The preview sources discuss revenue and EPS, not FCF. A lowered FCF guide or a capex raise would be new. If it were priced, the FY FCF guide would already have been trimmed, and it was maintained in August (https://quartr.com/events/fastly-inc-fsly-q2-2026_3gNKaFWt).
findings.independence: The revolver upsizing comes from the 8-K summarised at https://massive.com/quote/fsly. Memory and opex headwinds are in the Zacks preview (https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:2a43909f5094b:0-fastly-set-to-report-q3-earnings-what-s-in-the-cards-for-the-stock/).

findings.finding: The 22% fall in the last 5 sessions (to $21.04 from about $27 a week earlier) is a sector selloff, not company news. StockStory attributes the 6.7% fall on 2026-11-02 to software stocks extending a selloff on AI-capex fears (Oracle's $20bn raise, Alphabet and Amazon FCF) after the Nasdaq's worst month in over a year. Fastly filed only 10b5-1 insider sales and a Vanguard 13G/A in that span, and there were no analyst cuts. The bar has been reset into the print without a change in the company's numbers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In May 2026 the stock ran into the print at highs and fell 38%. This time it enters 37% below its 52-week high after a drawdown, the opposite setup. The tape has 82 moves of more than 5% in a year, so a sector-driven 22% fall is within its noise.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown is the market pricing a sector, so a company-level print that holds the guide can recover part of it. Puts are only mildly bid (skew +4.5), which means the options market does not treat the fall as an informed seller. If informed selling were behind it, skew would be extreme and short interest would have built; it fell from 21.19M to 20.58M.
findings.independence: EDGAR filing list (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001517413&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40) shows no 8-K since the 2026-10-08 date notice. This is a macro-to-company inference, sized small.

findings.finding: Fastly's own network data show AI request volume grew about 30% from January to May 2026, 6.5 times human traffic, and more than half of AI requests needed origin access. The Q2 10-Q says 'autonomous agent consumption is driving the bulk of internet traffic', and Other/Compute revenue grew 69% on AI-related customer requirements, which supports usage-based network services volumes in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The AI-traffic narrative drove the Feb 2026 +72%. In April 2026 the same AI theme cut the other way: Fastly fell 18% on Anthropic's managed agents launch (https://webhosting.today/2026/04/13/anthropics-managed-agents-launch-sent-fastly-down-18-akamai-12-and-extended-cloudflares-selloff).
findings.why_not_priced: This is a traffic proxy running to May only, and it is public, so mostly priced. It is filed because it is the only usage series available before Q3 closed.
findings.independence: The 10-Q MD&A (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001517413/000151741326000213/fsly-20260630.htm) is the same company. This is a proxy.

Cloudflare's Q3 2026 report is listed by aggregators for 2026-11-05 after hours (unconfirmed by the company), so its read-through also falls after the window.

baseline_tension: The skew (+4.5, puts bid) and the -22% run-in both point down. A sector-driven reset and a likely beat point modestly up, against a reaction history that has sold the last two beats, so the net is near flat and p_up is held at 52.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the beat finding cut from +1.0 to +0.5 and the guidance raise from +1.0 to +0.8, because the last two beat-and-raise prints were sold (-38%, -13%).
Rule 5 (proxies and macro transmission): the sector-reset positioning finding cut from +1.5 to +1.0 and the AI-traffic proxy from +0.5 to +0.3.
Rule 7 (positioning): with short interest at about 13% and 3.7 days to cover, the concentration negative was shrunk from -1.5 to -1.2.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the revolver upsizing is signed neutral because NRR and RPO corroborate the network ramp; the FCF-guide risk stays and was cut from -1.0 to -0.8.
Rule 6: Akamai and Cloudflare read-throughs are kept in outside_window.
